heroHeadline: S&P 500 Closes Week at 7,398.93 — Six-Week Winning Streak; Warsh Senate Vote May 11, Trump-Xi Summit May 14-15, Powell Expires May 15: Most Consequential 5-Day Macro Window of 2026
heroSubtitle: May 9: Markets enter the most consequential week of 2026 with the S&P 500 at 7,398.93 (six-week winning streak — longest since 2024; Nasdaq at 26,247.08) after the April BLS jobs beat (+115K vs ~60K consensus, released May 8) reduced recession probabilities: Goldman ~20%, JPMorgan ~25%, Moody's ~40%. Three simultaneous events converge May 11-15: (1) Kevin Warsh Senate floor vote (~92% confirmation probability; first meeting as Chair: June 9-10 FOMC); (2) Trump-Xi Beijing summit with Iran, tariff de-escalation, and rare-earth controls on agenda — Iran focus may crowd out tangible progress from the current 104%/84% bilateral barrier; (3) Powell's term expires May 15. Iran ceasefire nominally intact but US naval forces fired on Iranian tankers May 8 attempting Hormuz evasion — Trump insists ceasefire is still in effect; oil closes week at ~$101 Brent (still 50% above pre-war $67 WTI). Core PCE remains 3.2% (March, hottest since Iran war began), ISM Services Prices Paid 70.7 (highest since 2022) — the stagflation backdrop that constrains any Warsh-era easing. On May 9 (Russia's Victory Day), Trump announced a 72-hour Russia-Ukraine ceasefire with 1,000 prisoner swap per side — a positive geopolitical tail-risk reduction ahead of the summit. Section 122 tariff cliff July 23 (75 days) is the next structural deadline: no Congressional extension bill introduced. The Warsh era begins under a complex inheritance: growth adequate (+2.0% Q1 GDP, +115K jobs), inflation too high (PCE 3.2%), oil elevated (~$101 Brent), and the most consequential bilateral summit of the year five days away.
